newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears P&O/Nedlloyd container merger.
newsitem.headline: EU clears P&O/Nedlloyd container merger.

text.p: The European Commission said it had cleared the merger of the container shipping interests of P&O and Royal Nedlloyd, creating the world's third largest container operator and Europe's second largest.

Nedlloyd shareholders also gave their blessing on Friday to the new company, to be called P&O Nedlloyd Container Line Ltd, after a $1.5 billion deal announced in September which is due to become operational at the start of 1997.
"The new company...can therefore now proceed as planned from 1 January 1997," Nedlloyd said in a statement from Rotterdam.
Shares in the Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company (P&O) were at 591 pence by 1430 GMT, up six pence, while shares in Royal Nedlloyd NV were at 46.40 guilders, up 0.40.
The Commission said it had examined the effects of the joint venture on shipping routes to or from European ports where both P&O and Nedlloyd had container activities.
"The combined market share of P&O and Nedlloyd exceeds 20 percent only on the northern Europe-Australia/New Zealand route," it said in a statement.

The Commission said it had also considered the effect on liner conferences -- groups of vessel operators which apply uniform conditions on a route -- operating on the routes to or from European ports.
P&O is a member of all of the conferences operating on those routes and Nedlloyd of most of them.

"The Commission has considered that no dominance arises from the reduction of the number of members of any of the conferences on the routes examined or from the increase in the market share of a conference resulting from the merger," it said

The new company will have more direct ports of call and a wider range of trade routes than any other operator. It will boast an annual turnover of almost $4.0 billion and a net asset value of $1.5 billion.
The European Commission also said the new company will be a member of either the Global or Grand shipping alliances. But it did not say which camp P&O Nedlloyd Container Line Ltd would choose.
The merged entity would have to choose between the two, it said, although it looked more like a logical development of the merger than a condition imposed by the EU's competition watchdog.
"It is intended that the joint venture company will be a member of only one of these consortia," it said, noting that the alliances imposed notice periods which prevent immediate withdrawal.
